7360.title: Concurrent server startup removes another live server's pending fork
7360.rootCauseOneLine: Server startup does not acquire data-directory ownership before migrations and recovery; recovery treats every copying fork as abandoned, even while another server is alive.
7360.proposedFix: Introduce atomic OS-backed lifetime ownership before database initialization, retain it until all server work stops, and release it on startup failure and shutdown. Reuse the shared native-lock implementation rather than adding a second dependency or relying on a racy PID probe.
7360.caveats: Seeded in-progress fork state, not a live provider transfer. Queued-claim impact is source-supported only. No automatic PR: the available OS-backed lock is private to the shared configuration subsystem and scoped to short file mutations. Safely reusing it needs a new shared locking contract plus server-lifecycle integration, beyond this rule's one-existing-subsystem limit. A PID-only probe would leave simultaneous-start races and standalone servers uncovered.
